sector_model: Medical device: segment growth, gross and operating margin on adjusted and GAAP bases, FCF after SBC, IPR&D and acquisition accounting
thesis: Edwards Lifesciences (NYSE: EW), transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), transcatheter mitral and tricuspid therapies (TMTT) and surgical valves. Q3 2026 10-Q (0001099800-26-000054) and earnings release Exhibit 99.1 (0001099800-26-000053), both filed 2026-11-04. Q3 sales 1,715.5M (+10.5%, +11.2% constant currency): TAVR 1,241.6M (+8.0%), TMTT 209.5M (+44.3%), surgical 264.4M (+2.5%). Nine month sales 5,105.1M (+13.5%). Q3 GAAP EPS 0.53 vs adjusted 0.80 (+19%); GAAP includes a 220.2M impairment of an acquired IPR&D asset (218.4M IPR&D), excluded from adjusted; 9M GAAP also has a 163.6M loss on impairment of investments and 418.5M tax provision. Adjusted operating margin 30.3% vs GAAP 17.4%; gross margin 78.5% GAAP. 2026 guidance raised: sales growth about 11.5% cc, TAVR +9-9.5%, TMTT 780-790M, adjusted EPS 2.97-3.05, Q4 sales 1.67-1.75B, adjusted EPS 0.61-0.69. TTM (FY2025 10-K plus 9M26 minus 9M25, XBRL): net income 1021.3M (GAAP EPS about 1.78, 60x), OCF 1716.9M, capex 292.8M, FCF 1424.1M, SBC 172.8M. Shares 575.0M (10-Q cover 2026-10-31), market cap about 61.6B at 107.15; FCF yield 2.3% (2.0% after SBC); 35.6x the adjusted EPS guide midpoint of 3.01. Balance sheet 2026-09-30: cash 3,110.8M, short-term investments 1,533.9M, long-term investments 262.6M, long-term debt 598.8M, so net cash about 4.3B (EV about 57.3B). Buybacks 714M in 9M26, 1.3B authorization left. Market view: stock about 85 on 2026-10-14 (Investing.com snippet, unverified) and 107.15 now implies the market already pays for durable low double digit growth and margin expansion. Evidence for the company's case: TMTT momentum and three guidance raises; evidence against cheapness: 2% FCF yield. What closes the gap: TAVR volume growth above 9% with TMTT scaling, FCF conversion rising toward net income.
counterthesis: Price near a high multiple leaves little room: 36x adjusted EPS and 2% FCF yield. TAVR growth guided mostly from procedure volume rather than share gains, and competitors (Medtronic, Abbott, Boston Scientific) in TAVR and mitral/tricuspid could take share. Adjusted EPS excludes recurring acquisition related impairments (220M this quarter, 163.6M investment losses in 9M), so adjusted results overstate owner earnings. GAAP EPS fell to 1.61 from 1.67 for nine months while sales grew 13.5%. Gross margin guided at the low end of 78-79%. TMTT growth depends on reimbursement coverage, and the effective tax rate guided high end of 16-19%. Legal matters and the 10-K audit matters were not read; peer multiples and history were not compared; the Q3 stock reaction was not measured from verified prices.
invalidation: Thesis fails if TAVR growth falls below about 6%, TMTT growth stalls, adjusted operating margin guidance is cut, further impairments show acquired assets underperform, or the multiple compresses without earnings growth.
